Subject: Quarter kickoff — goal anchoring and exec commitment cascade

Team —

We're kicking off the quarter with a short, focused ask: anchor the top-line goals so we can lock exec commitments and finalize the QBR packet. Attached is v3 of the goal-anchor deck (high-level objectives + proposed metrics). Key asks: 

- Review the three proposed company OKRs on slides 2–4.
- Confirm whether the targets are stretch vs. baseline (put a quick note in the deck or reply).
- Tell me whether your org can commit to these metrics by EOD Tuesday (2028-04-03).

I want a single source of truth before Grace starts assembling the external QBR packet. If helpful, I'm proposing a 30-min sync — Thu 04/04 10:00–10:30 PT; calendar invite below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bOKR-Proposal
QBR packet draft (Notion): https://www.notion.so/rw/Quarterly-QBR-Packet-138b
Attachment: Q2_goal-anchor-draft-v3.pptx

Thanks — please be concise so Grace can move quickly.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

Marcus —

Thanks for the deck. Quick Qs before I confirm commit:

1) Objective 2 (Model latency SLO) — is the baseline the 90th percentile latency over last 30 days or last 7 days? That changes the uplift required.
2) For Objective 3 (cost/unit) — which clusters are in scope (hosted only, or dedicated + private)?

If those two definitions are explicit I can confirm a commitment by EOD Tuesday. I also left two comments on slide 3 about phrasing ("reduce" vs "improve").

Good catches. Quick answers: 

1) Latency SLO baseline = 90th pct over last 30 days (we'll call that baseline). I'll update the deck language to be explicit.
2) Cost/unit scope = hosted + dedicated (exclude private deployments for now; we'll surface as a separate initiative).

I've pushed those two clarifications to slide 3 and added short notes on stretch vs baseline (slide 4). Please re-check.

Grace — can you start the QBR packet assembly this afternoon once people start to land firm commitments? Vanessa — heads-up that Karthik will likely flag headcount assumptions for engineering resourcing.

Quick note —

I can support the goals but want to flag headcount assumption on slide 5: the deck assumes +6 FWEs in infra by mid-quarter. Karthik, can you confirm if that's feasible without shifting other roadmap commitments? If not, I'd propose we soften the "commit" language and mark it as "contingent on hiring cadence" so execs are aware.

Also looping procurement (procurement@acme.com) for visibility on any external contractual lead times for tooling that may affect the cost/unit metric (cc'd below).

Subject: Final: Quarter kickoff — goal anchoring and exec commitment cascade (decisions & sign-off)

Thanks everyone — summary and decisions below. Please reply with a one-line "+1" to confirm sign-off; if you need a caveat, include it in the same reply so Grace has it for the decisions log.

Decisions (final):
- Objective 1: "Platform reliability" — keep target as proposed (SLA success metric). Commitment: +1 from Kimberly, Vanessa.
- Objective 2: "Model latency" — baseline = 90th pct over last 30 days. Target = 15% improvement vs baseline. Commitment: +1 from Kimberly.
- Objective 3: "Cost per inference" — scope limited to hosted + dedicated clusters. Target = 10% unit cost reduction. Commitment: +1 from Vanessa; contingent note on tooling lead times added.
- Headcount note: engineering hires required (+6 FWEs) marked as "contingent on hiring cadence" per Vanessa's ask — not a blocker for exec readout. Karthik to provide hiring ETA by 4/10.

Attachments: Q2_goal-anchor-draft-v3.pptx (finalized with clarifications)
Notion (decisions log + packet): https://www.notion.so/rw/Quarterly-QBR-Packet-138b
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bOKR-Proposal

Grace — please proceed to finalize the external packet and flag anything you need from me.

If you accept the summary, reply with a single-line "+1".

—Marcus
